column1: # One row per interrupting compatible enabled on any of the boards (and per board member's
# compatible), read from the driver source at dccb0959: which interrupts it
# connects, where each priority comes from, and whether it changes enable state or
# priority after initialisation; envelope is the most conservative statement of those
# changes. Attestation, never proof: an inlined register write is not visible here.
# A row applies only when its driver's Kconfig symbol is set; the inventory (Task 10)
# treats an interrupting node whose rows name a driver symbol the .config does not set
# as not connected -- the driver is not compiled -- and a node with no row at all as
# unknown, which refuses the build. `irq_source none` says the driver connects none;
# applies_when `always` is a row with no predicate (no driver at all in the tree).
# A compatible may have several rows, one per configuration of its driver, told apart
# by applies_when; two rows applying under one configuration make the node unknown.
